Revision 17 writes D142-D144 into R4, R42, R43 and P15; no id, form or risk tag changes.
R4: the set-aside rule is judged match by match, from the longest down; FPS CASH DEPOSIT STRIPE | STRIPE is ambiguous (verify-73; T03 4b3b21c builds it).
R42/P15: a save whose head record is not taken back answers not confirmed (D143). R43/P15: a holder's read and a busy-gate read count only while their lock files are the case's, and interference before a read is outside what a reader can know (D144; T12 0d339cc, 3076547).
Not written: D148's 'the take-back checks only the head record'. Under lock-file interference it lets a take-back unrecord a repair told recorded, against R42's own guarantee. R42 keeps the lock re-check, which answers not confirmed and also settles verify-72's third finding. One question.
Build impact: none for T03's R4; under the default, T12 turns the take-back's lock re-check back on and changes one test.

questions.context: D148 asks R42 to say that the take-back checks only that the head record is still the save's own, as T12's 0d339cc builds. Written so, R42 contradicts its own guarantee under lock-file interference. Save A passes its re-check before its head rename, and the case lock file is replaced. Repair B takes the new lock and finds A's line torn; a person confirms dropping it; B renames the repaired log and passes its re-check before its head rename. A's head record lands, A's read-back finds its entry gone, and the take-back's head check passes. B's head record lands, and B reads back an intact log and is told recorded. The take-back's rename then puts back the older head record. B's entry is now past the recorded entries as a torn write, and a confirmed drop leaves an intact log without a save told recorded. A take-back that re-checks the lock files finds the replaced case lock and is not made, so A is not confirmed (D143), which also answers verify-72's third finding. Revision 17 keeps that re-check. Which should R42 say?
options: Keep the lock re-check on the take-back, as on every head rename; a take-back it stops answers not confirmed (design default; R42 stays satisfiable; T12 turns one check back on and changes the test at tests/test_case_log.py:2401 before its review)

Check only the head record, as D148 asks and 0d339cc builds, and write into R42's guarantee that under lock-file interference a take-back can leave the entry of a repair told recorded past the recorded entries, where a confirmed drop then removes it

Name the take-back tests (:2275, :2401, :2423) and the eight added since review 20 p15.

T03, before its review (D147): no R4 change is needed for revision 17, since 4b3b21c builds D142. Fix the recurring minors: README.md:78 (thirteen reviews), the TypeError for an unhashable id or a list pattern (:441, :469), and RETURNED DD reversal linking (:997).

P15: a schedule in which a repair under lock-file interference publishes its head record between a take-back's head check and its rename; the log must read broken, or intact with the repair's save, never intact without it.

requirements.md.new:
Revision 17, after D148 (changes requested under the owner's standing approval of 2026-11-19, after T12's twenty-fourth review, verify-72, and T03's twenty-third, verify-73; the owner had answered revision 16's questions as D142 to D144). R4, R42, R43 and P15 change; their ids, forms and risk tags do not. R4 now says that a match set aside inside a longer listed phrase sets nothing aside even when its rule counts by another match elsewhere in the line. Matches are settled from the longest down, so whether a match counts rests only on the longer matches that hold it, and a rule counts, and is among the candidates, where any match of its own counts (D142). With FPS CASH DEPOSIT STRIPE listed as a cash paid-in phrase and FPS CASH DEPOSIT and STRIPE as a gateway's names, FPS CASH DEPOSIT STRIPE | STRIPE is ambiguous, with the rail, the cash paid-in rule and the gateway as its candidates, not a cash deposit (verify-73). R42 and P15 now name a third answer, not confirmed, for a save whose read-back fails and whose head record is not then taken back. Such a save is neither recorded nor not recorded, and asks for the case log to be checked before anything else is saved, which shows whether its entry is among the recorded entries (D143). So that the two answers do not meet, R42's and P15's 'a writer refused after its line' now reads 'refused after its line and before its head record is published', and a repair may remove the entry of a save reported as not confirmed as it may one reported as not recorded. R43 and P15 now say which lock files each reader counts on. A reader that holds the case, sign-off included, counts on the case lock it holds and the gate it passed, and across a removed or replaced one it reads again as a reader that does not hold the case. A reader that finds the gate busy counts on the case lock it holds shared, and any other reader on the gate it holds and the case lock behind it (D148, after verify-72). They also say that lock-file interference beyond a read across such a lock file is outside what a reader can know, and that a check made after it stops gives the true answer (D144). One term, not confirmed, is new. D148 also asks R42 to say that the take-back checks only that the head record is still the save's own, as T12's 0d339cc builds. Revision 17 does not write that clause, because R42 would then contradict its own guarantee that, under lock-file interference, a log that reads intact holds every save told recorded. In this schedule it fails. A save passes its re-check before its head rename, and the case lock file is replaced. A repair takes the new lock, finds the save's line torn and, once a person confirms it, renames the repaired log and passes its re-check before its head rename. The save's head record lands, its read-back finds its entry gone, and the take-back finds the head record its own. The repair's head record lands, the repair reads back an intact log and is told recorded, and the take-back's rename puts back the older head record. The repair's entry is then past the recorded entries as a torn write, and once a person confirms dropping it, the log reads intact without a save told recorded. A take-back that re-checks the lock files first, as every head rename does, finds the replaced case lock and is not made; the save is then not confirmed, which also answers verify-72's third finding. R42 therefore keeps the take-back's rename among the steps a writer re-checks both case lock files before, and revision 17 asks the owner. Every other requirement, property, term and id is as revision 16 left it.

requirements.md.new:
A reader's read SHALL count only while the lock files it counts on are still the case's lock files. A reader that holds the case, sign-off included, counts on the case lock it holds and the gate it passed to take the case; a reader that finds the gate busy and holds the case lock shared counts on that case lock; and any other reader counts on the gate it holds through the read and on the case lock behind it, whether it holds that case lock shared or finds it held. IF one of them was removed or replaced during the read, THEN the reader SHALL take the read again, as a reader that does not hold the case if it held the case, and SHALL claim nothing from the read across it; IF that happens on every attempt within its retries, THEN the reader SHALL claim nothing about any entry.
Scope (revision 17): beyond a read across a lock file the reader counts on, lock-file interference is outside what a reader can know. A lock file removed or replaced before the reader's read leaves the lock files the reader counts on the case's, while a writer that passed the old gate can still take the case through it, so the reader may report being saved over an entry another writer left incomplete, or report a live append as incomplete. A check made after the interference stops gives the true answer.

- The lesson is D108's, in R4: a reviewer reads a requirement's noun at the grain the requirement defines it, and R4 defines a match at one start.

**What the owner decided on revision 16** (D142-D145, D148, 2026-11-20)
- D142 answered revision 16's first question with its default: R4's set-aside rule is judged match by match. A match set aside inside a longer phrase sets nothing aside, even when its rule counts by another match, and matches are settled from the longest down. The owner built it in 4b3b21c (the section after next).
- D143 answered the second with its default: a save whose read-back fails and whose head record cannot be taken back is not confirmed, neither recorded nor not recorded, and asks for the case log to be checked. The owner built it in 3076547 (SaveNotConfirmed).
- D144 answered the third with its default: R43 and P15 say that, beyond a read across a lock file the reader holds, lock-file interference is outside what a reader can know, and that a check made after it stops gives the true answer. It needs no build change.
- D145 approved revision 16. D148: write D142 to D144 into the requirements. State in R43 that a holder's read and a busy-gate read count only while the lock files are still the case's, and in R42 that the take-back checks only that the head record is still the save's own (0d339cc). Keep everything else in revision 16. Revision 17 writes all of it but the take-back clause, which would contradict R42's guarantee (next section), and asks the owner about that clause.

**What T12's twenty-fourth review showed** (verify-72; D146, D148, 2026-11-20)
- verify-72, T12's twenty-fourth review, judged the owner's f5436bb against revision 16 and failed P15 on three majors. First, the read revision 16 named as open: a check that found the gate busy and held the case lock shared returned its read without comparing that lock file with its path. With the case lock replaced during the read and entry 2 appended under the new one, the check reported entry 2 missing (src/cma/case.py:530 there). Second, a reader that held the case returned its read without comparing the lock files it took. With the case lock replaced during the read and entry 2 appended through another handle under the new one, the holder reported entry 2 missing from its stale read (:459 there). Third, the take-back reused the head record's publication, whose lock re-check refused it. With the gate replaced just after a save's head record was published and a one-shot read error in the read-back, the save said it was not recorded, and a fresh check read the log intact with its entry, which no repair could drop (:1006 there). Three minors recur: the producer claimed exit 0 with 'appending' for a held torn tail, where the contract test expects exit 4 and 'being saved'; the stress test does not force the interleaving claimed for it; and the claim's suite totals and diff-stat describe an earlier patch.
- The owner built 0d339cc and then 3076547, neither yet reviewed; D146, the unblock, is pending. In 0d339cc a holder's read counts only while the case lock it holds and the gate it passed are still the case's, and otherwise goes on as any other reader's. The busy-gate read compares the case lock it holds with its path, and the take-back checks only that the head record is still the save's own, whatever the lock files. In 3076547 a save whose take-back is not made, because the head record is no longer its own or cannot be read or renamed, raises SaveNotConfirmed. Four tests mark them: a busy-gate read and a holder's read across a replaced case lock, each taken again (tests/test_case_log.py:2355 and :2380, named p15), a take-back made through a replaced lock file (:2401), and a take-back not made, answering not confirmed (:2423); the last two are marked invariants but not named p15.
- The first finding is R43 as revision 16 wrote it. The second turns on which lock files a holder holds: it holds the case lock and passed the gate, and D148 writes both into R43.
- D143 alone answers the third finding. With the take-back's lock re-check kept, verify-72's schedule ends with the save not confirmed, which P15 allows since revision 17, and the case log check then shows its entry among the recorded entries. 0d339cc goes further and drops the re-check, which reopens a schedule the re-check closed:
  - A writes its line and passes its re-check before its head rename. The case lock file is replaced.
  - B takes the new lock and finds A's line torn. A person confirms dropping it, and B renames the repaired log and passes its re-check before its head rename, since the head record still lists what both checks read.
  - A's head record lands. A's read-back finds its entry gone, and its take-back's check finds A's head record.
  - B's head record lands over A's. B reads back an intact log that holds its drop entry and is told recorded.
  - The take-back's rename then puts back the head record A's check read. B's drop entry lies past the recorded entries as a torn write, and once a person confirms dropping it, the log reads intact without a save told recorded, which R42 rules out.
  With the re-check, the take-back finds the replaced case lock and is not made; A is not confirmed, and the log reads intact with B's save. Revision 17 keeps the re-check and asks the owner (Options considered).
- Still open at 3076547. A failed staging write or fsync of a head record or a repaired log still leaves its temporary file (src/cma/case.py:966-971, :906-911). A refusal in the second call of a short write of the line still says nothing was written, though part of the line is on disk (:1008, :797-798). Eleven tests added since review 20 are marked invariants but not named p15 (tests/test_case_log.py:2070-2423), which the project's gotcha asks for.
- The lesson is revision 10's, turned round: a check removed to answer one schedule can reopen the one it closed. Where a requirement already gives the refused step an honest answer, the check stays.

**What T03's twenty-third review showed** (verify-73; D142, D147, D148, 2026-11-20)
- verify-73, T03's twenty-third review, judged the owner's 5c9a5bd and 2c72469 against revision 16 and failed R4 on one major, the corner revision 16 asked about. With FPS CASH DEPOSIT STRIPE added to the cash list and FPS CASH DEPOSIT to the gateway list beside STRIPE, FPS CASH DEPOSIT STRIPE | STRIPE was a cash deposit recorded as v2:cash_paid_in, in trading receipts. The trailing STRIPE kept the gateway counting, so its FPS CASH DEPOSIT, set aside inside the cash phrase, still set aside the rail (src/cma/categorise.py:820 there). The reviewer expects the credit unexplained, with the rail, the cash rule and the gateway as candidates. Four minors, all recurring. README.md:78 still says naming the payer in the profile can clear an ambiguous credit, the thirteenth review to find it. The producer claimed the rule-order shuffle for debits, which take the first protected match by design (IWOCA DIVIDEND). An unhashable rule id raises a TypeError (:441). And the claim's compileall covers evals and tests, which the runner does not compile.
- D142 took revision 16's default, and the owner built it in 4b3b21c, not yet reviewed; D147, the unblock, is pending. Each occurrence counts on its own: an occurrence is set aside when it lies inside a strictly longer occurrence of another rule that itself counts, the bank's code and the cash and payment-method pair exempt as before, and a rule counts while any occurrence of it does (credit_matches, src/cma/categorise.py:805-844 there). It repeats the filter over the occurrences until the set it keeps stops changing, rather than sorting them by length. Since an occurrence's standing rests only on strictly longer occurrences, the repetition reaches the one answer that settling from the longest down gives. One test marks it: with XYZ FPS a gateway's name and XYZ FPS CASH DEPOSIT a cash phrase, XYZ FPS CASH DEPOSIT REF XYZ FPS is ambiguous, with the rail and the cash rule among its candidates (tests/test_rules_v2.py:1910). No shipped phrase holds both cash wording and a payment-method cue, so no shipped verdict moves.
- D148: write D142 into R4, keeping everything else; revision 17 does that.
- Still open at 4b3b21c: README.md:78; the TypeError for an id or a pattern given as a list (:441, :469); RETURNED DD reversal linking, whose bank prefixes (:997) still hold UNPAID DD but not RETURNED DD; and the reversal-linking time, which T22's timed recompute (R52) should include.
- The lesson is revision 16's, finished: a match's standing is its own, and the rule it belongs to lends it none.

**Sub-decision: what a take-back checks before its rename (revision 17, after verify-72; D148 asks for the head record alone; design default, asked).** The take-back is a head rename (revision 16). verify-72 replaced the gate after a save published its head record and failed the read-back with a one-shot read error. f5436bb's take-back re-checked the lock files and refused, and the save said it was not recorded while its head record listed its entry. (i) Re-check both lock files and the head record before the take-back's rename, as before every head rename, and answer not confirmed when either check stops it (D143); verify-72's schedule then ends not confirmed. (ii) Check only that the head record is still the save's own, whatever the lock files, as 0d339cc builds and D148 asks R42 to say. (iii) Make no take-back, and answer not confirmed whenever a read-back fails. *Design default: (i)*, asked in revision 17. (ii) loses to the schedule in Context (T12's twenty-fourth review). A repair that checked before the save's head record landed publishes its own head record after the take-back's check and is told recorded; the take-back then lands over it, and a later confirmed drop leaves an intact log without that repair's save. R42 rules that out, so (ii) would need a second exception in R42's guarantee, beside D124's. Under (i) the repair holds the case only through a replaced case lock, which the take-back's re-check finds. A writer that takes the case after that re-check checked a head record that lists the save's entry, so its own entry follows that entry. A take-back that then lands over its head record leaves two or more entries past the recorded ones, and the log reads broken, never intact. (iii) lost because a read error alone, with no interference, would leave the save not confirmed where a take-back makes it plainly not recorded. What (i) costs: under interference, a failed read-back after a lock file was replaced answers not confirmed, and the person checks the case log before saving again. T12 turns the lock re-check back on for the take-back, and its test that a take-back goes through a replaced lock file (tests/test_case_log.py:2401) expects not confirmed instead.
